title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the 11th Batch of Guiding Cases

articles.content_en:
I. Whether the franchise right of a sewage treatment project may be pledged

The franchise right of a sewage treatment project is the right to operate and maintain a sewage treatment plant and obtain corresponding revenues. The operation and maintenance of a sewage treatment plant constitute the operator's obligations, while the right to receive revenues constitutes the operator's right. Since the operation and maintenance of a sewage treatment plant are not transferable property rights, the pledge of the franchise right of the sewage treatment project in dispute is in substance the pledge of the revenue right of the sewage treatment project.

As to whether the revenue right under franchise operations such as sewage treatment projects may be pledged, the following aspects shall be considered: First, the Franchise Operation Right Pledge Guarantee Agreement in respect of the sewage treatment project in dispute was executed in 2005. Although at that time, laws, administrative regulations, and relevant judicial interpretations did not provide that the revenue right of a sewage treatment project may be pledged, the revenue right of a sewage treatment project is similar in nature to the revenue right of a highway. Article 97 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China provides that "if the revenue right of immovable property such as highway bridges, highway tunnels, or highway ferries is pledged, the matter shall be handled in accordance with the provisions of Article 75(4) of the Guarantee Law," which clarifies that highway revenue rights are other rights that may be pledged according to law, and thus the similar revenue right of sewage treatment shall also be allowed to be pledged. Second, the Implementation Opinions on Certain Policies and Measures for the Development of the Western Region issued by the State Council's Office of the Leading Group for the Development of the Western Region and forwarded by the General Office of the State Council on September 29, 2001 (Guo Ban Fa [2001] No. 73) proposed that "for water conservancy development projects and urban environmental protection projects (such as urban sewage treatment and garbage treatment) that have certain repayment capacity, the business of granting loans secured by project revenue rights or charging rights shall be explored and gradually initiated," which for the first time explicitly allowed trial implementation of pledging the revenue right of a sewage treatment project. Third, although the revenue right of a sewage treatment project is a future monetary claim, its exercise period and the amount of revenue can be determined, and it is a definite property right. Fourth, after the promulgation and implementation of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Property Law), since the revenue right of a sewage treatment project is a future monetary claim arising from the provision of sewage treatment services, it may by its nature fall within the scope of "accounts receivable" that may be pledged according to law. Therefore, the revenue right of the sewage treatment project in dispute, as a specific property right, may be allowed to be pledged.

II. Publicity of the pledge of the revenue right of a sewage treatment project

With respect to the publicity of the pledge of the revenue right of a sewage treatment project, after the Property Law came into force on October 1, 2007, since the revenue right has been included in the scope of "accounts receivable" under Article 223(6) of that Law, the pledge shall be registered in the accounts receivable pledge registration publicity system of the Credit Reference Center of the People's Bank of China for the pledge right to be established according to law. Since the pledge guarantee agreement in this case was executed in 2005, before the Implementation of the Property Law, the unified registration system for accounts receivable under the Property Law is not applicable. Because there were no unified registration publicity provisions at that time, by reference to the then regulations on the registration of pledges of highway toll collection rights, record filing registration was made with the competent authority, and interested parties could inquire with the competent authority whether the revenue right was subject to a pledge, and such right had the effect of real right publicity.

In this case, the Changle City Construction Bureau affixed its seal to the Franchise Operation Right Pledge Guarantee Agreement, and Article 7 of the Agreement explicitly stipulated that "the Changle City Construction Bureau agrees to handle the pledge registration and pledge delivery registration procedures for the plaintiff and Fuzhou Municipal Engineering Company," so it may be determined that the competent authority of the sewage treatment project in dispute had knowledge of and approved the pledge of the right, and interested parties could also inquire with the Changle City Construction Bureau about the pledge of the relevant rights of the sewage treatment plant in dispute. Therefore, the pledge of rights in dispute in this case has satisfied the requirements for publicity, and the pledge right has been established.

III. Method of realizing the pledge of the revenue right of a sewage treatment project

Neither the Guarantee Law nor the Property Law of China specifically provides for the specific method of realizing a pledge of rights, but only makes general provisions on the realization of a pledge right, i.e., when exercising the pledge right, the pledgee may enter into an agreement with the pledgor to discount the pledged property, or have priority in compensation from the proceeds from auction or sale of the pledged property. However, the revenue right of a sewage treatment project is a future monetary claim, and the pledgee may request the court to order it to directly collect money from the pledgor's debtor and exercise priority in compensation over such money, so there is no need to adopt the method of discount, auction, or sale. Moreover, revenue rights are always subject to certain burdens, and the operating entity is specific, so by their nature, auction or sale is also inappropriate. Therefore, the plaintiff's request to auction or sell the pledged property under the Franchise Operation Right Pledge Guarantee Agreement and exercise priority in compensation shall not be upheld.

According to the agreement, the plaintiff, Wuyi Sub-branch of Strait Bank, has the right to directly collect sewage treatment service fees from the Changle City Construction Bureau and exercise priority in compensation over the collected sewage treatment service fees. Since the defendant is still obliged to operate and maintain the sewage treatment plant normally in accordance with the agreement, if normal operation cannot be ensured, it would affect the sewage treatment in the urban area of Changle City, and would also affect the plaintiff's collection of sewage treatment fees. Therefore, when the plaintiff collects sewage treatment service fees from the Changle City Construction Bureau, it shall exercise its rights reasonably and reserve the necessary and reasonable expenses for the defendant to operate the sewage treatment plant.

(Trial judges of the effective judgment: He Zhong, Zhan Qianghua, Zhu Honghai)

Guiding Case No. 54

Anhui Branch of Agricultural Development Bank of China v. Zhang Dabiao, Anhui Changjiang Financing Guarantee Group Co., Ltd. Dispute over Objection to Enforcement

(Deliberated and adopted by the Adjudication Committee of the Supreme People's Court, released on November 19, 2015)

Keywords: civil, action concerning objection to enforcement, pledge of money, specific identification, transfer of possession

Main Points of the Adjudication

Where a party opens a special margin account for the money pledged in accordance with the agreement, and the pledgee obtains control over possession of that special account, this satisfies the requirements for specific identification of money and transfer of possession. Even if the balance of funds in the account fluctuates, this does not affect the establishment of the pledge of money.

Relevant Legal Provisions

Article 212 of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China

Basic Facts

The plaintiff, Anhui Branch of Agricultural Development Bank of China (hereinafter referred to as ADBC Anhui Branch), alleged that it had cooperated with the third party, Anhui Changjiang Financing Guarantee Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Changjiang Guarantee Company), in credit guarantee business in accordance with the Credit Guarantee Business Cooperation Agreement executed between them. The funds in the guarantee margin special account opened by Changjiang Guarantee Company at ADBC Anhui Branch were in fact the pledge guarantee provided by Changjiang Guarantee Company to ADBC Anhui Branch. ADBC Anhui Branch requested a judgment confirming that it had a pledge right over the funds in that account.

The defendant, Zhang Dabiao, argued that the Loan Guarantee Business Cooperation Agreement between ADBC Anhui Branch and the third party, Changjiang Guarantee Company, did not contain an expression of intention to create a pledge; the funds in the account in question were themselves fluctuating, failing to meet the requirement of specific identification of money, and thus ADBC Anhui Branch did not have a pledge right over the funds in the margin account.

The third party, Changjiang Guarantee Company, agreed with ADBC Anhui Branch's view that it had a pledge right over the funds in the account.

The court found through trial: On April 7, 2009, ADBC Anhui Branch and Changjiang Guarantee Company executed a Loan Guarantee Business Cooperation Agreement. Article 3, "Guarantee Methods and Guarantee Liability," stipulated: Party A (Changjiang Guarantee Company) provided a guarantee to Party B (ADBC Anhui Branch) in the form of joint and several liability guarantee; the scope of the guarantee included the principal claim and interest, liquidated damages, and costs of realizing the claim. Article 4, "Guarantee Margin (Guarantee Deposit)," stipulated: Party A shall open a guarantee margin special account with Party B, and the bank for the guarantee margin special account shall be the Business Department of ADBC Anhui Branch, with the account number ending in 9511; Party A shall deposit the margin stipulated for the specific guarantee business into the guarantee margin special account before the guarantee contract is signed; the margin to be paid by Party A shall not be less than 10% of the loan amount; without Party B's consent, Party A may not use the funds in the guarantee margin special account. Article 6, "Collection, Extension, and Assumption of Guarantee Liability of Loans," stipulated: If the borrower fails to repay in full when overdue, Party A shall, within five days after receiving a written notice from Party B, assume the guarantee liability to Party B in accordance with Article 3 and transfer the corresponding funds to the account designated by Party B. Article 8, "Liability for Breach of Contract," stipulated: If the balance of the guarantee special account opened by Party A with Party B, for any reason, falls below the agreed amount, Party A shall make up the shortfall within three working days after receiving notice from Party B; before the shortfall is made up, Party B may suspend the business under this agreement. If Party A violates Article 6 of this agreement and fails to perform the guarantee liability on time, Party B has the right to deduct the corresponding funds from the guarantee fund special account or any other account opened by Party A with Party B. On October 30, 2009, and October 30, 2010, ADBC Anhui Branch and Changjiang Guarantee Company also executed two Credit Guarantee Business Cooperation Agreements similar in content to the above agreement.

After the execution of the above agreements, ADBC Anhui Branch and Changjiang Guarantee Company cooperated in loan guarantee business. Changjiang Guarantee Company opened a guarantee margin account with ADBC Anhui Branch, with the account number ending in 9511. Changjiang Guarantee Company paid the guaranteed proportion of guarantee margin in accordance with the agreement, and on that basis provided joint and several liability guarantee for the corresponding amount of loans. From April 3, 2009, to December 31, 2012, a total of 107 transactions occurred in this account, with credit transactions being the margin paid by Changjiang Guarantee Company; debit transactions mainly fell into two categories: one was the margin returned by ADBC Anhui Branch upon the application of Changjiang Guarantee Company after loan repayment, with part of the return going to the debtor's account; the other was the margin deducted by ADBC Anhui Branch from this account after a loan became overdue.

On December 19, 2011, during the trial of the case of Zhang Dabiao v. Anhui Liuben Food Co., Ltd., Changjiang Guarantee Company, et al. concerning a private lending dispute, the Hefei Intermediate People's Court, upon Zhang Dabiao's application, preserved funds in the amount of RMB 14,957,852 in the above margin account of Changjiang Guarantee Company. After the judgment in that case became effective, the Hefei Intermediate People's Court transferred RMB 13,383,132.57 from the above margin account to its own account. ADBC Anhui Branch, as a third party, raised an objection to enforcement, but on November 2, 2012, the Hefei Intermediate People's Court ruled to dismiss the objection. Subsequently, ADBC Anhui Branch filed this lawsuit due to the dispute over the objection to enforcement with the defendant Zhang Dabiao and the third party Changjiang Guarantee Company.

Adjudication Result

The Hefei Intermediate People's Court rendered a civil judgment on March 28, 2013 ((2012) He Min Yi Chu Zi No. 00505), dismissing ADBC Anhui Branch's claims. After the judgment was pronounced, ADBC Anhui Branch appealed. The Anhui Higher People's Court rendered a civil judgment on November 19, 2013 ((2013) Wan Min Er Zhong Zi No. 00261): 1. Setting aside the civil judgment of the Hefei Intermediate People's Court ((2012) He Min Yi Chu Zi No. 00505); 2. ADBC Anhui Branch has a pledge right over RMB 13,383,132.57 in the account of Changjiang Guarantee Company (account number ending in 9511).

Adjudication Reasoning

The effective judgment of the court held that the focus of dispute in the second instance was whether ADBC Anhui Branch had a pledge right over the funds in the account in question. This shall be examined from two aspects: whether a pledge relationship existed between ADBC Anhui Branch and Changjiang Guarantee Company, and whether the pledge right was established.

I. Whether a pledge relationship existed between ADBC Anhui Branch and Changjiang Guarantee Company

Article 210 of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Property Law) provides: "To create a pledge right, the parties shall conclude a pledge contract in writing. A pledge contract generally contains the following clauses: (1) the type and amount of the secured claim; (2) the time limit for the debtor to perform its obligations; (3) the name, quantity, quality, and condition of the pledged property; (4) the scope of the guarantee; and (5) the time for delivery of the pledged property." In this case, although no separate contract bearing the word "pledge" was executed between ADBC Anhui Branch and Changjiang Guarantee Company, based on the terms of Articles 4, 6, and 8 of the agreement, ADBC Anhui Branch and Changjiang Guarantee Company reached consensus through negotiation on the following matters: Changjiang Guarantee Company established a guarantee margin special account for the margin paid for guarantee business, and Changjiang Guarantee Company paid margin in a certain proportion of the loan amount; ADBC Anhui Branch, as the opening bank, obtained control over the margin deposited in that account by Changjiang Guarantee Company, and without its consent, Changjiang Guarantee Company could not freely use the funds in the account; if Changjiang Guarantee Company failed to perform its guarantee liability, ADBC Anhui Branch had the right to deduct the corresponding funds from the account. This consensus explicitly stipulated the type and amount of the secured claim, the time limit for debt performance, the quantity and delivery time of the pledged property, the scope of the guarantee, and the conditions for exercising the pledge right, thus containing the general terms of a pledge contract as required by Article 210 of the Property Law. Therefore, it shall be determined that a written pledge contract was concluded between ADBC Anhui Branch and Changjiang Guarantee Company.

II. Whether the Pledge over the Funds Involved in the Case Has Been Established
Article 212 of the Property Law stipulates: "A pledge shall be established upon the delivery of the pledged property by the pledgor to the pledgee." Article 85 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China provides that where a debtor or a third party, after specifying its funds in the form of a special account, sealed funds, security deposit, or the like, delivers possession thereof to a creditor as security for a claim, the creditor may be compensated out of such funds on a priority basis if the debtor fails to perform its obligation. Pursuant to the above provisions of law and judicial interpretation, funds, as a special type of movable property, may be used for pledge. As a special type of pledge over movable property, a pledge over funds differs from a mortgage over immovable property and a pledge over rights and shall also satisfy the two requirements of specification of funds and delivery of possession to the creditor, so that the funds are neither mixed with other property of the pledgor nor dependent on the property of the pledgee.
In this case, first, the funds were specified in the form of a security deposit. Changjiang Guarantee Company opened an account with Anhui Branch of Agricultural Development Bank of China on April 3, 2009, and the account number was consistent with that agreed upon in the Loan Guarantee Business Cooperation Agreement, i.e., the two parties had opened a special guarantee deposit account for the pledged funds as agreed upon in the agreement. After the special guarantee deposit account was opened, the funds transferred into the account were security deposits paid by Changjiang Guarantee Company into the account at a certain percentage of each guaranteed loan amount; the funds transferred out of the account were refunds and deductions of security deposits by Anhui Branch of Agricultural Development Bank of China. The account was not used for daily settlements, and therefore, it satisfied the requirement under Article 85 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China that funds shall be specified in the form of a special account, etc. Second, the specified funds were delivered into the possession of the creditor. Possession refers to the factual state of control and management over property. The guarantee deposit account involved in the case was opened with Anhui Branch of Agricultural Development Bank of China. Changjiang Guarantee Company, as the owner of the funds in the special guarantee deposit account, should have been entitled to freely withdraw funds therefrom; however, the Loan Guarantee Business Cooperation Agreement stipulated that without the consent of Anhui Branch of Agricultural Development Bank of China, Changjiang Guarantee Company shall not use the funds in the special guarantee deposit account. Meanwhile, the Loan Guarantee Business Cooperation Agreement stipulated that if the guaranteed loan was not repaid upon maturity, Anhui Branch of Agricultural Development Bank of China was entitled to directly deduct funds from the special guarantee deposit account. Anhui Branch of Agricultural Development Bank of China, as the creditor, obtained control over the guarantee deposit account involved in the case, and actually controlled and managed the account. Such transfer of control satisfies the requirement of delivery of pledged funds to the possession of the creditor. Accordingly, it shall be determined that the two parties had established a pledge over the funds in the guarantee deposit account involved in the case.
Regarding whether the fluctuation of account funds affects the specification of funds. The specification of security deposits in the form of a special account does not mean fixedness. In the process of using the account involved in the case, with the development of guarantee business, the balance of funds in the guarantee deposit account fluctuated. When a guarantee company carries out a new loan guarantee business, it is required to deposit a certain percentage of the guarantee amount into the account as agreed, which will necessarily lead to an increase in the account funds; when the loan guaranteed by the guarantee company is not repaid upon maturity, the deduction of funds from the guarantee deposit account will necessarily lead to a decrease in the account funds. Although the funds in the account fluctuated according to the business situation, they all corresponded to the guarantee business. Except for the deposited guarantee funds, the disbursed funds were all used for the refund and deduction of the guarantee funds, and were not used for daily settlements of non-guarantee business. That is, Anhui Branch of Agricultural Development Bank of China could control the account, and Changjiang Guarantee Company's use of the funds in the account was restricted. Therefore, the fluctuation of the account funds still satisfied the requirements of specification and delivery of possession for funds as a pledge, and did not affect the establishment of the pledge over the funds.
(Effective adjudicating judges: Huo Nan, Xu Xuhong, Lu Yuhe)

Guiding Case No. 55
Bai Wanqing v. Chengdu Nanxun Item Marketing Service Center et al. (Dispute over Infringement of Utility Model Patent)
(Discussed and adopted by the Adjudication Committee of the Supreme People's Court, released on November 19, 2015)

Keywords: Civil; Infringement of Utility Model Patent; Scope of Protection; Technical Terms; Infringement Comparison

Key Points of Judgment
The scope of protection of a patent right shall be clear. If the wording of the claims of a utility model patent right has obvious defects, and the specific meaning of the technical terms in the claims cannot be determined by combining the patent specification, drawings, common general knowledge in the art, and relevant prior art, resulting in the scope of protection of the patent right being obviously unclear, then it is impossible to conduct a meaningful infringement comparison with the accused infringing technical solution, and therefore the accused infringing technical solution cannot be found to constitute infringement.

Relevant Legal Provisions
Article 26(4) and Article 59(1) of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China

Basic Facts
The plaintiff, Bai Wanqing, was the patentee of a utility model patent with patent number 200420091540.7, titled "Anti-electromagnetic pollution suit" (hereinafter referred to as the patent-in-suit). The technical features of claim 1 of the patent-in-suit were: A. an anti-electromagnetic pollution suit, comprising an upper garment and a lower garment; B. a metal mesh or film with a shielding function is provided in the fabric of the garment; C. the metal mesh or film with a shielding function is composed of metal filaments or metal powder with high magnetic permeability and no residual magnetism. The patent specification stated that the purpose of the patent was to provide an anti-electromagnetic pollution suit with low cost, wide scope of protection, and good effect. It was characterized in that the garment is provided in the fabric with a metal mesh or film for shielding protection composed of metal filaments or metal powder with high magnetic permeability and no residual magnetism. The metal filaments may be commercially available copper filaments of 5 to 8 meters, etc., and the metal powder may be soft iron powder, etc. Figures 1 and 2 showed that the protective suit, without changing the style and fabric function of existing garments, is made by weaving conductive metal filaments into the fabric or compounding conductive metal powder with the fabric by any processing method such as spraying, coating, diffusion, soaking, and printing and dyeing, so as to form a mesh structure with mesh holes.
On May 28, 2010, Chengdu Nanxun Item Marketing Service Center sold an upper garment of the Tianxiang brand radiation protection suit produced by Shanghai Tianxiang Industrial Co., Ltd., at a price of 490 yuan, with the following technical features: a. an upper garment of an anti-electromagnetic pollution suit; b. a metal protective mesh with a shielding function is provided in the fabric of the garment; c. the metal protective mesh with a shielding function is composed of stainless steel metal fibers. On July 19, Bai Wanqing filed a civil action with the Chengdu Intermediate People's Court of Sichuan Province on the ground that the Tianxiang brand radiation protection suit upper garment (hereinafter referred to as the accused infringing product) sold by Chengdu Nanxun Item Marketing Service Center and produced by Shanghai Tianxiang Industrial Co., Ltd. infringed the patent-in-suit, seeking an order that Chengdu Nanxun Item Marketing Service Center immediately cease selling the accused infringing product; Shanghai Tianxiang Industrial Co., Ltd. cease producing and selling the accused infringing product, and pay damages of 1 million yuan.

Judgment
On February 18, 2011, the Chengdu Intermediate People's Court of Sichuan Province rendered the civil judgment (2010) Cheng Min Chu Zi No. 597, dismissing Bai Wanqing's claims. After the judgment was pronounced, Bai Wanqing appealed. On October 24, 2011, the Sichuan Higher People's Court rendered the civil judgment (2011) Chuan Min Zhong Zi No. 391, dismissing the appeal and affirming the original judgment. Not satisfied, Bai Wanqing applied to the Supreme People's Court for retrial, and the Supreme People's Court ruled on December 28, 2012 to dismiss his application for retrial.

Reasons for Judgment
The effective judgment of the court held that the disputed issue in this case was whether the accused infringing product produced by Shanghai Tianxiang Industrial Co., Ltd. and sold by Chengdu Nanxun Item Marketing Service Center infringed Bai Wanqing's utility model patent for the "Anti-electromagnetic pollution suit." Article 26(4) of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "The claims shall be supported by the description and shall clearly and concisely define the scope of patent protection sought." Article 59(1) provides: "The scope of protection of an invention or utility model patent shall be determined by the content of the claims. The description and drawings may be used to interpret the content of the claims." It can be seen that accurately defining the scope of protection of a patent right is a prerequisite for determining whether the accused infringing technical solution constitutes infringement. If the wording of the claims has obvious defects, and even after combining the patent specification, drawings, common general knowledge in the art, and relevant prior art, the specific meaning of the technical terms in the claims still cannot be determined, and the scope of protection of the patent right cannot be accurately determined, then the accused infringing technical solution cannot be subjected to a meaningful infringement comparison with the claims. Therefore, for a patent right with a clearly unclear scope of protection, the accused infringing technical solution cannot be found to constitute infringement.

In this case, it was difficult to determine the specific range of "high magnetic permeability" in technical feature C of claim 1 of the patent-in-suit. First, according to the evidence provided by Bai Wanqing, although magnetic permeability is sometimes referred to as magnetic conductivity, magnetic permeability includes absolute magnetic permeability and relative magnetic permeability, and depending on specific conditions, concepts such as initial magnetic permeability μi and maximum magnetic permeability μm are also involved. Different concepts have different meanings and different calculation methods. Magnetic permeability is not constant; when the magnetic field intensity H changes, a change in magnetic permeability can be observed. However, in the specification of the patent-in-suit, it was not stated whether magnetic permeability in the technical solution of the patent-in-suit refers to relative magnetic permeability or absolute magnetic permeability or other concepts, nor was the specific range of high magnetic permeability stated, nor were the objective conditions for calculating magnetic permeability, including magnetic field intensity H, stated. It was difficult for a person skilled in the art to determine the specific meaning of "high magnetic permeability" referred to in the patent-in-suit based on its specification. Second, from the relevant evidence submitted by Bai Wanqing, although it could prove that some prior art did use expressions such as high magnetic permeability and high magnetic conductivity, depending on the technical field and magnetic field intensity, the meaning of so-called high magnetic permeability was very broad, ranging from 80 Gs/Oe to 83.5×104 Gs/Oe all referred to as high magnetic permeability by Bai Wanqing. The evidence provided by Bai Wanqing could not prove that in the technical field to which the patent-in-suit pertains, persons skilled in the art had a relatively unified understanding of the meaning or range of high magnetic permeability. Finally, Bai Wanqing argued that depending on the specific environment of use, a person skilled in the art could determine a specific safe lower limit and thus determine the required magnetic permeability. This argument essentially sought to include all situations that could achieve the purpose of radiation protection within the scope of protection of the patent-in-suit, which was too broad and lacked factual and legal basis.

In summary, based on the specification of the patent-in-suit and the relevant evidence provided by Bai Wanqing, it was difficult for a person skilled in the art to determine the specific range or specific meaning of "high magnetic permeability" in technical feature C of claim 1, and the scope of protection of claim 1 could not be accurately determined, making it impossible to conduct a meaningful infringement comparison between the accused infringing product and the claim. Therefore, the judgment of the second instance finding that Bai Wanqing failed to prove that the accused infringing product fell within the scope of protection of the patent-in-suit was not erroneous.
(Effective adjudicating judges: Zhou Xiang, Luo Xia, Du Weike)

Guiding Case No. 56
Han Fengbin v. Inner Mongolia Jiujun Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. et al. (Dispute over Objection to Jurisdiction in Product Liability Dispute)
(Discussed and adopted by the Adjudication Committee of the Supreme People's Court, released on November 19, 2015)

Keywords: Civil Action; Objection to Jurisdiction; Period of Retrial

Key Points of Judgment
If a party fails to raise an objection to jurisdiction within the period for filing a statement of defense at first instance, and raises an objection to jurisdiction at second instance or at retrial or upon remand for retrial, the People's Court shall not examine it.

Relevant Legal Provisions
Article 127 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China

Basic Facts
In a case concerning a dispute over product quality damages brought by the plaintiff Han Fengbin against the defendants Inner Mongolia Jiujun Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jiujun Pharmaceutical), Shanghai Yunzhou Commercial Building Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yunzhou Commercial Building), Shanghai Broadcasting and Television Station (hereinafter referred to as Shanghai TV Station), and Dalian Hongyan Pharmacy Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hongyan Pharmacy), the Dalian Intermediate People's Court of Liaoning Province rendered the civil judgment (2007) Da Min Quan Chu Zi No. 4 on September 3, 2008. Jiujun Pharmaceutical, Yunzhou Commercial Building, and Shanghai TV Station were dissatisfied and appealed to the Liaoning Higher People's Court. The court rendered the civil judgment (2008) Liao Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 400 on May 24, 2010. After this judgment became legally effective, the applicants for retrial, Jiujun Pharmaceutical and Yunzhou Commercial Building, applied to the Supreme People's Court for retrial.
On December 22 of the same year, the Supreme People's Court rendered the civil ruling (2010) Min Shen Zi No. 1019, deciding to bring the case up for trial, and on August 3, 2011, rendered the civil ruling (2011) Min Ti Zi No. 117, setting aside the judgments of first and second instance and remanding the case to the Dalian Intermediate People's Court of Liaoning Province for retrial. During the retrial, Jiujun Pharmaceutical and Yunzhou Commercial Building raised an objection to jurisdiction.

Judgment
On February 29, 2012, the Dalian Intermediate People's Court of Liaoning Province rendered the civil ruling (2011) Da Shen Min Zai Chu Zi No. 7, holding that the court's retrial of this case was pursuant to the instruction of the Supreme People's Court, and that one of the defendants, Hongyan Pharmacy, had its domicile in Zhongshan District, Dalian City, Liaoning Province, and thus ruled to dismiss the objection to jurisdiction raised by Jiujun Pharmaceutical and Yunzhou Commercial Building. Jiujun Pharmaceutical and Yunzhou Commercial Building appealed. On May 7, 2012, the Liaoning Higher People's Court rendered the civil ruling (2012) Liao Li Yi Min Zai Zhong Zi No. 1, holding that when the plaintiff Han Fengbin filed the action with the Dalian Intermediate People's Court, he had already listed Hongyan Pharmacy, which had its domicile in Dalian City, as one of the defendants, and during the original trial had submitted relevant evidence of purchasing medicine from Hongyan Pharmacy which was examined and cross-examined at trial; Hongyan Pharmacy was a proper defendant, and the Dalian Intermediate People's Court had jurisdiction over the case. The court thus dismissed the appeal and affirmed the original ruling. Jiujun Pharmaceutical and Yunzhou Commercial Building later applied separately to the Supreme People's Court for retrial. On March 27, 2013, the Supreme People's Court rendered the civil ruling (2013) Min Zai Shen Zi No. 27, dismissing the applications for retrial of Jiujun Pharmaceutical and Yunzhou Commercial Building.

Reasons for Judgment
The effective judgment of the court held that with respect to the period for a party to raise an objection to jurisdiction, Article 127 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Civil Procedure Law) clearly provides: "If a party objects to the jurisdiction, it shall raise the objection within the period for filing a statement of defense. If a party fails to raise an objection to jurisdiction and responds to the action and defends, it shall be deemed that the court accepting the action has jurisdiction." It can be seen that if a party fails to raise an objection to jurisdiction within the period for filing a statement of defense at first instance, and only raises an objection to jurisdiction at second instance or during retrial, then, under the principle of jurisdictional constancy, the jurisdiction over the case has already been determined, and the People's Court shall not examine it. In this case, Jiujun Pharmaceutical and Yunzhou Commercial Building raised the objection to jurisdiction only during the retrial before the court of first instance after the case was remanded for retrial by a ruling through the trial supervision procedure. At the initial first instance, the plaintiff Han Fengbin's complaint was served on Jiujun Pharmaceutical and Yunzhou Commercial Building, and they did not raise any objection to jurisdiction within the response period, indicating that they had accepted the jurisdiction of the court of first instance, and the jurisdiction had been determined. Moreover, the case had gone through first instance, second instance, and retrial, and the procedures passed through still have procedural validity and are irreversible. This case was remanded to the court of first instance for retrial through the trial supervision procedure. Although it was tried in accordance with the first-instance procedure, a case remanded for retrial is not a new trial; the jurisdiction over the case had already been determined. As far as jurisdiction is concerned, since the initiation of civil litigation procedures begins with the party's filing of the action, the determination of jurisdiction over a case shall be based on the time of filing. The court that has jurisdiction over a case at the time of filing shall not be affected by changes in the facts that determine jurisdiction during the course of the litigation. When a case is filed with a People's Court and the court accepts the case and serves the complaint on the defendant, and the defendant does not raise an objection to jurisdiction within the response period, it indicates that the court with jurisdiction over the case has been determined. Thereafter, the court with jurisdiction over the case shall not be changed due to changes in the party's domicile, habitual residence, or changes in administrative divisions. Under the premise that jurisdiction has been determined, the party no longer has the right to raise an objection to jurisdiction. If during a retrial a party could still raise an objection to jurisdiction, it would undoubtedly put the already stable litigation procedure in an uncertain state, undermining the stability and order of the litigation procedure, delaying the proceedings, not only reducing litigation efficiency and wasting judicial resources but also being detrimental to the resolution of disputes. Therefore, based on the principle of jurisdictional constancy, the certainty of litigation procedures, and the requirements of justice and efficiency, an objection to jurisdiction raised again by a party in a retrial case cannot be supported. Accordingly, the objections to jurisdiction raised by Jiujun Pharmaceutical and Yunzhou Commercial Building in this case lacked legal basis, and the original ruling dismissing their objections to jurisdiction was not erroneous.

In summary, the applications for retrial of Jiujun Pharmaceutical and Yunzhou Commercial Building did not satisfy the circumstances for granting a retrial under Article 200(6) of the Civil Procedure Law. Therefore, in accordance with Article 204(1) of that Law, it was ruled to dismiss the applications for retrial of Jiujun Pharmaceutical and Yunzhou Commercial Building.
(Effective adjudicating judges: Zhang Zhihong, Ning Sheng, Jia Yaqi)
